key_insights.title: Mechanism
key_insights.body: one-dimensional channels decorated with adjacent uncoordinated carboxylate-O atoms → selectivity

key_insights.title: Mechanism
key_insights.body: adjacent uncoordinated carboxylate-O atoms along the channels → selectivity

key_insights.title: Design Rule
key_insights.body: [positive] introduce a non-polar pore surface when seeking stronger C2H6 preference → a non-polar surface favors C2H6 adsorption

key_insights.title: Design Rule
key_insights.body: [positive] tailor the pore surface chemical environment and pore size to a sweet spot that simultaneously favors C2H2/C2H4 and C2H6/C2H4 selectivity → enables simultaneous high selectivities for both C2H2/C2H4 and C2H6/C2H4 in one-step C2H4 purification

key_insights.title: Comparison
key_insights.body: pure C2H4 breakthrough behavior and productivity under humid environment vs pure C2H4 breakthrough behavior and productivity under dry environment: winner=tie on breakthrough_behavior_and_productivity

notable_quotes: C2H2 occupies the primary sites near two adjacent carboxylate-O atoms in Cage C, while C2H6 prefers sites in Cages A and D; C2H2 binds more strongly in Cage C.
Breakthrough tests directly produced polymer-grade (>99.95%) C2H4 from binary feeds and from ternary mixtures including 34/33/33 and 1/90/9 compositions.
Adjacent uncoordinated carboxylate-O atoms are the key binding sites that preferentially recognize C2H2 and C2H6 over C2H4 in HIAM-210.
